image_reading: A dark, rigid foreground ride structure contains multiple suspended seats and visible rider silhouettes facing a large projected prehistoric landscape.
One projected pterosaur is already airborne near the upper-right area of the screen, with wings extended and a rider-like figure visible on its back.

The projected pterosaur’s wing articulation supports limited airborne motion, but its exact flight direction is ambiguous; the seats, rails, supports, silhouettes, and screen boundary provide no evidence of safe mechanical movement.
analysis.article_context: Body image illustrating the immersive Jurassic-world flight attraction “На крыльях ветра,” supporting the article’s promise of one-ticket access to vivid, adventurous experiences and introducing the recommended park routes.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Convey the attraction’s immersive sensation of a fantastic flight through a Jurassic world.
structured_intent.initial_state: One projected pterosaur is airborne near the upper-right portion of the visible screen with wings extended, while the foreground seats, rails, supports, and rider silhouettes are stationary.
structured_intent.primary_action: The projected pterosaur performs one restrained wingbeat while drifting slightly inward within the existing screen.
structured_intent.attention_anchor: The single projected pterosaur, continuously visible within the existing screen and clear of the upper-right crop.
structured_intent.motion_boundary: Only the projected pterosaur’s existing wings and its position within the current screen may change slightly; the foreground seats, riders, rails, supports, attachments, screen boundary, and all other visible scenery remain source-locked, with no added ride rows, objects, or off-screen space.
structured_intent.terminal_state: The pterosaur remains fully visible farther inward from the upper-right crop, airborne with its wings extended after the restrained wingbeat.
structured_intent.geometry_invariant: The foreground seats, rails, supports, and their existing attachment points retain their rigid shape and mutual arrangement; the projected-screen boundary stays fixed.
structured_intent.identity_invariant: Exactly one projected pterosaur and the exact existing count of visible seats, structural details, rider silhouettes, people, and limbs are preserved.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The scene remains an immersive Jurassic flight-attraction experience, with the pterosaur airborne and the foreground ride assembly intact through the final frame.
structured_intent.feasibility_assessment: The pterosaur is visibly airborne with articulated wings, supporting a restrained wingbeat or slight inward drift; its exact travel direction is ambiguous. No movement is safely evidenced for the foreground ride structure, seats, or riders.

models.scene_plan: Across four seconds, the projected pterosaur begins from its existing wings-extended airborne pose, performs one restrained down-and-up wingbeat at an even pace, and shifts only slightly inward from the upper-right edge. The camera remains fixed with zero screen travel. Near the end, the wings settle into an extended glide pose while the pterosaur stays continuously visible; every foreground seat, rider silhouette, rail, support, attachment point, and the existing projected-screen boundary remains rigid and unchanged, and no new structure or scenery is introduced.
models.positive_prompt: The projected pterosaur makes one slow, shallow wingbeat in place, then drifts slightly inward while remaining fully inside the existing screen and clear of the upper-right crop. Keep the camera fixed and all foreground seats, riders, rails, supports, attachment points, and the screen boundary rigid; it ends airborne with wings extended, with no added ride rows or objects.
